answer: The distribution of the RNA expression data in COAD__geneExp.xls is **HIGHLY RIGHT-SKEWED**. On the pooled raw as-provided distribution (all 20,502 genes × 328 samples = 6,724,656 values), the Fisher–Pearson sample-corrected moment skewness is g1 ≈ **42.44** (population form 42.44), far above the |g1| ≥ 1 "highly skewed" threshold and with heavy right tail (mean 932 vs median 177; max 1.34×10⁶; ~15.2% zeros). Robustness checks agree: Pearson median-based 3(mean−median)/SD ≈ 0.57, per-gene-mean layer g1 ≈ 15.1, per-gene-median layer ≈ 16.1, per-sample-mean layer ≈ 1.31, and zeros-excluded raw g1 ≈ 39.5 — all right-skewed; a bootstrap 95% CI for g1 (≈18.6–34.3 on a 200k subsample) lies entirely above 1. Caveat (transform-dependent only): the file is provided on a RAW non-log2 scale; applying log2(x+1) would instead give g1 ≈ −0.30 (approximately normal) and log2(nonzero) g1 ≈ −0.69, but that is a transformed layer and does NOT change the primary classification of the data as provided.
